answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring each identity to forge a stake-backed reputation over time: a new agent posts a bond and must do verifiable work before its votes count. Like water carving a karst landscape, trust forms slowly through costly actions rather than cheap registration, so an attacker pays the same price for every fake identity. A relic of past good behavior, an auditable history of completed tasks, is expensive to fake at scale, because each clone needs its own bond, work, and time. The cost per identity, not the detection rate, makes the attack unprofitable.
